text: 14. This unusual fly is frequently encountered by hunters and hikers in North America and Europe during the early fall. Upon finding a suitable host, the insect performs a strange ritual: it snaps off its own wings to settle in permanently for a long-term blood meal. Its bites are known to cause intense itching and irritation that can persist for several weeks. Name this insect.

15. This microscopic mite is a close relative of the common eyelash mite but chooses a slightly different niche. It bypasses the hair follicles to live deeper within the skin, specifically inside the sebaceous glands that produce natural oils. They remain hidden during the day and only emerge onto the surface at night to find a mate before returning to their oily environment. What is this specific species?
